elements.element: Vendor defends Customer against third-party claims
elements.evidence: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim

elements.element: Trigger: allegation that services or deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right

elements.element: Trigger: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor
(d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct
20.4 ... shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim
tender control of its defence and settlement
provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: 20.3 ... arising out of content Customer provides to the Services in violation of a third party's intellectual property rights ... Customer has no other indemnification obligation

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (modifications, combinations, specifications)
elements.evidence: 20.2 ... Customer's unauthorized modification ... combination ... Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications

elements.element: Infringement remedies: procure, modify, replace, refund
elements.evidence: 20.5 ... procure the right ... modify or replace it ... Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap language appears; 21.3 merely lists indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims with no 3× annual fees ceiling.

offending_extra_words: The indemnifying party may not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party without its prior written consent.
The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense, and delayed notice relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced.
procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item
Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated portion and Fees paid for items Customer can no longer reasonably use
reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present and operative: Vendor defence/indemnity for Customer and Affiliates across the four required triggers, notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a Customer indemnity confined to Customer content and Customer's breach of law.
The fallback bargain is incomplete because no 3× annual fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity is inserted, but the locked target is preferred, so this is not disqualifying.

Minimality fails: the insertion adds hold-harmless language, a Customer defence duty, settlement-consent/participation/material-prejudice mechanics beyond notice-control-cooperation, and the fallback-level procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, none of which are required by the preferred prose.

Intent is preserved: unrelated sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 remain untouched and effective, defined terms (Affiliate, Applicable Law, Customer Data, Deliverable, Vendor Technology, Fees) are all resolved, and the previously dangling cross-reference in 9.3 to Section 20.5 now resolves; the heading-anchor placement should nevertheless be re-anchored after the preceding section's final body paragraph.
